correctness.rationale: Accepted edges are sampled uniformly from vacant edges, so while a,b,c remain, the rare-event chance is bc/[a(b+c)+bc]. Each accepted majority/minority edge lowers s=b+c by one; B-C lowers s by two and increments J, leaving exactly M−S+2J unpaired A. Since a>=M−S and bc<=(b+c)^2/4, each minority-minority event has p<=s/[4(M−S)]; the expected number is O(S²/M)=o(S) and J/S→0. Conditional B fraction has drift only on B-C events, equal p(b−c)/[s(s−2)], and the rest is a bounded-difference martingale, establishing uniform bulk composition. Coupling to Bernoulli intensities (BC/S²)(S−k)/M has total-error o(S²/M); these sum to BC/(2M)(1+O(1/S)). Le Cam proves finite-λ Poisson convergence, while compensator variance and martingale variance O(λ) give the diverging-λ law. An independently coded exact recursive finite-state absorption law was normalized/symmetric in 54 small triples; at (M,B,C)=(100,10,10), E J=0.49767 near the critical prediction 0.5.
residual_risks: The finite exact-law tests corroborate the model but do not establish total-variation limits; the martingale/coupling bounds are the actual large-scale argument.
Hypotheses require both minority sizes of order n and M/n→∞; neither balance at fixed M/n nor other adsorption protocols is covered.

Broader random greedy matching asymptotics do not automatically yield the critical Poisson law with explicit rate BC/(2M) for the specific dominant-class depletion process. Searches did not locate an exact equivalent; possible implicit generalized density-dependent Markov-chain theorem remains a material priority risk.

value.rationale: The Poisson-to-law-of-large-numbers transition for rare successful minority–minority pairings identifies a natural sharp n² majority-size crossover, and the exact vacancy relation interprets the defect count as the jamming correction. This is a motivated stochastic phase phenomenon, not an artificial finite-parameter count.
residual_risks: Poisson approximation requires M scaling at least quadratically to keep λ finite; there is no claim for weakly dominant class or nonuniform edge attempt rates.

final_claim: For random greedy dimer adsorption on K_{M,B,C} with M/n→∞, B/n→α>0, C/n→β>0, the number J of successful minority–minority B-C dimers is asymptotically Poisson when BC/(2M)→λ finite and satisfies J/(BC/(2M))→1 in probability when the parameter diverges; final majority vacancies are M−(B+C)+2J.
